You know these folks chose this topic just so they could get funding to live in Hawaii and pretend to be real scientists. It's funny the number of research topics that occur near tropical resorts...

Trust me, it's not all fun and games, last week it got so cold at night I had to go dig up a blanket. There are reasons for doing research here:

  • it's relatively isolated yet also accessible (there are monsanto corn fields here...the need for isolation of these fields by thousands of miles of ocean is a little too suspect for me tho...). Barring potential sketchy shit, agricultural research can be conducted here year round.

  • There are also 9 distinct climates on the Big Island alone. Lots of potential for conducting simultaneous research into things that require exploration in different climates without the need to fly all over the world or wait for seasons to change.

  • There is very little light pollution for astronomical research, even going as far as using sodium street lights on the B.I.

  • People from all over the world congregate here and provide their own unique views. Forget being a melting pot, we're more of a salad bowl: distinct and separate yet working together. This is both great in general as well as a topic of interest for sociological research.

  • There's an active volcano that you can walk up to if you're doing geological research.

  • etc.

I agree, some people do take advantage of a free vacation, but there is legitimacy for doing work here.
